## Result

For each fixed closed oriented genus g ≥ 2, every pair of points in every original closed Teichmüller ball admits a continuous rectifiable path inside that same ball of length at most its ambient distance plus 4c_g. Consequently N_g(k) = k + 4c_g for every fixed k > 0, including the distance-two bound 2 + 4c_g. The metric is the actual half-log-dilatation Teichmüller metric. The constant depends only on genus; no numerical or uniform-in-genus value is claimed.

## Mathematical evidence and attribution

This draft contains the full authored proof, its byte-identical audited version, and the full byte-identical independent AI mathematical audit. The audit reports PASS with no blocking mathematical finding. The public proof applies exactly its two optional editorial suggestions, documented in the README: identify Theorem 15 as the extremal-length part of Theorem A, and use “Consequently” before the intrinsic-distance bound.

The substantive Teichmüller input is Anna Lenzhen and Kasra Rafi, [*Length of a curve is quasi-convex along a Teichmüller geodesic*, JDG 88 (2011), 267–295](https://www.math.toronto.edu/rafi/Papers/Convexity.pdf), Theorems C and 17. The added general metric argument retreats endpoints before invoking the uniform additive quasiconvexity theorem and then concatenates three geodesic pieces. Published geodesic existence is also used.

This is an AI mathematical audit, not human peer review or formal proof-assistant verification. No historical novelty or priority is claimed. One substantive approach was used out of a limit of five. The theorem is a theoretical deduction; no substantive computational experiment was required or used as mathematical evidence. Hashes, sizes, file comparisons, and patch replay are publication-integrity checks only.

## Exact scope

Add only the eight files listed below under `unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/11000026/`. The package contains proof, audit, acceptance/status, public source metadata, and an exact file manifest. It contains no executable scripts, test fixtures, copied third-party source documents, dataset contents, private sources, or private coordination material. No QUEUE.md or unrelated repository changes are included.
